standard_prerequisites.name: Feller Markov operators, controllability, coupling, Hilbert-space analysis and standard measure inequalities
standard_prerequisites.use: The original hypotheses H1-H4, cited standard facts and all source-local coupling arguments are retained.

core_obligations: The author converts approximate controllability and a dense linearized noise response into an asymptotic coupling with high-probability stabilization, controls accumulated changes of noise law, and combines stability with recurrence to obtain uniform mixing.
difficulty_reason: The author converts approximate controllability and a dense linearized noise response into an asymptotic coupling with high-probability stabilization, controls accumulated changes of noise law, and combines stability with recurrence to obtain uniform mixing.

dedup.scope: Shared existing-claims baseline has no JEP130 addition. Public1934 counts a stability transfer theorem assuming high-probability stabilization and noise-law control; t1.1 instead derives those properties from controllability and concludes unique stationarity and uniform convergence.

compared.difference: Conditional dual-Lipschitz stability transfer versus construction of the coupling from H1-H4 and uniqueness/uniform mixing of the stationary law.
